You are offered a local authority or AHB tenancy in order of priority/time on the list

documents_required.doc: Proof of income for all household earners
Proof of identity and right to reside in Ireland

eligibility.income_note: Max household NET income for a single person: EUR40,000/yr in Band 1 local authorities (value shown); EUR35,000 Band 2; EUR30,000 Band 3; plus 5% per additional adult (max 10%) and 2.5% per child.

programmes.source_snippet: Social housing income eligibility thresholds are the net income thresholds below which a person is entitled to social housing supports (i.e. social housing or the Housing Assistance Payment).

programmes.funder: Approved Housing Bodies / Land Development Agency (Department of Housing)
programmes.amount_note: Rent set at a minimum 25% below open-market rents in the area, linked to the cost of delivering and maintaining the home; tenancy is long-term with strong security
programmes.deadline_note: Homes are advertised when available (e.g. on AHB/LDA websites); applications are open for a limited window per development

procedure_steps.detail: Watch for cost rental homes advertised by Approved Housing Bodies or the LDA in your area

Apply online during the advertised window, showing your net household income is below the Cost Rental income limit (€66,000 Dublin / €59,000 elsewhere) and that you are not in receipt of other State housing support

documents_required.doc: Proof of household income (Revenue Employment Detail Summary or payslips)
Photo ID and proof of address

eligibility.income_note: Net household income limit EUR59,000/yr outside Dublin (value shown) and EUR66,000/yr in Dublin.

programmes.source_snippet: your net household income is below €66,000 per year if applying for a tenancy in one of the four Dublin Local Authority areas and below €59,000 per year if applying for a tenancy anywhere else in Ireland

programmes.name_local: Local Authority Home Loan (Iasacht Tithíochta Údaráis Áitiúil)
programmes.funder: Local authorities (funded by Housing Finance Agency)
programmes.amount_note: Government-backed mortgage at fixed rates: 4.00% fixed for up to 25 years (APR 4.07%) or 4.05% fixed up to 30 years (APR 4.13%); you can borrow up to 90% of the market value of new or second-hand homes

procedure_steps.detail: Check eligibility and property price ceilings on localauthorityhomeloan.ie
Submit your application form with income and mortgage documentation to your local authority
Sign up to the local authority collective Mortgage Protection Insurance scheme

documents_required.doc: Completed Local Authority Home Loan application form
Proof of income and employment (payslips, Revenue documents)
Bank statements and proof of deposit

eligibility.income_note: Maximum gross annual income €80,000 for a single applicant and €85,000 for joint applicants (increases effective 1 April 2026). Two years continuous employment for the primary earner.

programmes.source_snippet: as a single applicant have an annual gross income of not more than €80,000 (gross). as joint applicants have an annual gross income of not more than €85,000 (gross)

programmes.name_local: First Home Scheme (Scéim na gCéad Tí)
programmes.funder: First Home Scheme Ireland DAC (State and participating banks)
programmes.amount_note: Shared equity support of up to 30% of the market value of a new home (20% if also using Help to Buy); minimum 2.5% of the price or €10,000, whichever is higher; no service charge for the first 5 years, then 1.75%/2.15%/2.85% tiers

procedure_steps.detail: Check your eligibility and the property price ceiling for your local authority area on firsthomescheme.ie
Get mortgage approval from a participating lender (AIB, EBS, Haven, Bank of Ireland or PTSB)
Register and apply online; the FHS pays its share at closing in return for an equity stake you can buy back later

documents_required.doc: Mortgage approval from a participating lender
Proof of identity and first-time-buyer status
Property details within the local price ceiling

eligibility.income_note: No income limit. Citizens Information (2026) publishes no income ceiling for the First Home Scheme; constraints are the first-time-buyer/new-build rules, the standard 4x gross income mortgage borrowing limit, and property price ceilings of €375,000 to €500,000 depending on local authority area and property type.

programmes.source_snippet: You can get up to 30% of the market value of your new property with the First Home Scheme. This is reduced to 20% if you are also getting the Help to Buy Scheme.

programmes.name_local: Help to Buy Scheme (Scéim Cabhrú le Ceannach)
programmes.amount_note: Refund of Income Tax and DIRT paid over the previous 4 tax years, capped at €30,000 or 10% of the purchase price, whichever is lower; for first-time buyers of new-build homes priced up to €500,000 (self-builds included)
programmes.deadline_note: Enhanced relief (up to EUR30,000) applies to applications up to 31 December 2029. Approval must be in place before you draw down the mortgage

procedure_steps.detail: Check your estimated refund using the HTB calculator in Revenue myAccount
Apply through myAccount once you have signed contracts, giving mortgage and property details
The refund is paid to your solicitor on closing and used towards your deposit

documents_required.doc: Mortgage approval of at least 70% of the property value
Signed contract for the new-build property
Tax clearance / full tax compliance for the 4 previous years

eligibility.income_note: Not means-tested, but the refund cannot exceed the Income Tax and DIRT you actually paid in the 4 previous tax years

programmes.source_snippet: Help to Buy (HTB): refund of Income Tax and DIRT from the last 4 years, up to €30,000 or 10% of the price, for first-time buyers of newly-built homes under €500,000

programmes.name_local: Vacant Property Refurbishment Grant (Deontas Athchóirithe Maoine Folmhaí)
programmes.funder: Local authorities (Croí Cónaithe (Towns) Fund, Department of Rural and Community Development)
programmes.amount_note: Up to €50,000 to refurbish a property vacant for at least 2 years, plus a €20,000 top-up if the property is derelict (€70,000 total); up to €60,000/€84,000 on off-shore islands; plus up to €5,000 for conservation advice on traditional houses
programmes.deadline_note: The grant must be approved before any work begins

procedure_steps.detail: Apply to your local authority with the application form and proof the property has been vacant for 2+ years and was built before 2008
Get tax clearance from Revenue and provide quotes for the refurbishment works
The local authority approves the grant; works are inspected before payment

documents_required.doc: Proof of ownership or contract of purchase
Evidence of vacancy for at least 2 years

eligibility.income_note: Not means-tested; you must live in the refurbished home as your principal residence or rent it out (RTB-registered); not available to companies or developers

programmes.source_snippet: You can get a grant of up to: €50,000 to renovate a vacant property; €70,000 if the property is derelict. The grant must be approved before any work begins.

programmes.name_local: Housing Adaptation Grant for People with a Disability
programmes.name_en: Housing Adaptation Grant for People with a Disability (HAG)
programmes.amount_note: Means-tested local authority grant; maximum EUR40,000 or 100% of approved costs (whichever is less) for homes over 12 months old (max EUR20,000 for newer homes); income bands: 100% <= EUR37,500, tapering to 30% at EUR62,501-75,000

procedure_steps.detail: Apply to your local authority with the grant application form and an occupational therapist's report on the adaptation needed
Provide quotes and proof of household income for the means test
Local authority approves and inspects the works before payment

eligibility.income_note: Household income up to EUR37,500 qualifies for 100% of costs; grant tapers (85%/75%/50%/30%) up to EUR75,000/yr household income (value shown); no grant above EUR75,000.

programmes.source_snippet: A grant is not available if the household income is more than €75,000, after the disregards and deductions are applied.

programmes.amount_note: Fast-track grant of up to EUR8,000, which may cover 100% of the cost of mobility works (grab rails, ramps, accessible shower, stairlift)

procedure_steps.detail: Apply to your local authority describing the mobility aids needed
Provide proof of household income; the local authority assesses and inspects

eligibility.income_note: Household annual gross income must be below EUR37,500 (all household members aged 18+ assessed, previous tax year).

programmes.source_snippet: The Mobility Aids Grant covers up to €6,000 towards basic works to address mobility issues in the home

programmes.name_local: Housing Aid for Older People Grant
programmes.name_en: Housing Aid for Older People Grant
programmes.amount_note: Means-tested grant up to EUR10,700 or 100% of costs for essential repairs (roof, wiring, heating, doors/windows) for people aged 66+; 100% if household income <= EUR37,500, tapering to 30% at EUR62,501-75,000

procedure_steps.detail: Apply to your local authority with proof of age, income and ownership/tenancy
Local authority assesses priority and means, and inspects the completed works

eligibility.income_note: Household income up to EUR37,500 qualifies for 100% of costs (max grant EUR10,700); tapers to 30% at EUR62,501-75,000 (value shown = cut-off); no grant above EUR75,000.

programmes.source_snippet: The Housing Aid for Older People Grant is for people aged 66 and over and provides up to €10,700 for essential home repairs; means-tested based on household income

programmes.name_local: SEAI Individual Home Energy Upgrade Grants (Better Energy Homes)
programmes.name_en: SEAI Home Energy Upgrade Grants (insulation, heat pumps, windows)
programmes.amount_note: Individual SEAI grants (maximum per measure): attic insulation EUR2,000 (EUR2,500 for first-time buyers and homeowners on qualifying welfare payments); wall insulation EUR8,000; windows EUR4,000; external doors EUR1,600; heat pump system EUR14,500 (includes Renewable Heat Bonus); heating controls EUR700; solar PV EUR1,800; battery storage EUR600 flat rate; solar water heating EUR1,200
programmes.deadline_note: You must apply and receive grant approval BEFORE any work begins; works must be done by an SEAI-registered contractor

procedure_steps.detail: Choose an SEAI-registered contractor and get a quote
Apply online on the SEAI portal before works start and wait for your Letter of Offer
Complete works with a post-works BER assessment and submit declarations for payment

documents_required.doc: Post-works Building Energy Rating (BER) where required

eligibility.income_note: Not means-tested for standard grants; homes generally must have been built and occupied before 2011 (insulation/heating controls) or before 2021 (heat pumps/renewables)

programmes.source_snippet: Heat pump grant nearly doubled — the maximum heat pump grant rose from €6,500 to €12,500 for houses (€9,500 for apartments); includes a €4,000 Renewable Heat Bonus and up to €2,000 for central heating upgrades

programmes.amount_note: €700 per kWp for the first 2 kWp and €200 per additional kWp up to 4 kWp; maximum €1,800 for a 4 kWp+ domestic solar PV system (2026)
programmes.deadline_note: Apply before installation; you must receive a Letter of Offer from SEAI before works begin

procedure_steps.detail: Choose an SEAI-registered solar PV company and agree system details
Apply on the SEAI portal before any installation work and wait for approval
After installation, submit the Declaration of Works, Safe Electric certificate, NC6 form and post-works BER for payment

eligibility.income_note: Not means-tested; open to homeowners and private landlords; home must have been built and occupied before 2021; new installations only

programmes.source_snippet: The maximum domestic solar PV grant remains €1,800 in 2026: €700 per kWp up to 2 kWp, then €200 per additional kWp from 2 kWp to 4 kWp

programmes.name_local: Warmer Homes Scheme (Scéim Tí níos Teo)
programmes.amount_note: Fully funded (free) home energy upgrades for eligible energy-poor households — typically attic and wall insulation, draught proofing, lagging jackets, heating upgrades and, where suitable, deeper retrofit measures
programmes.deadline_note: There can be a significant waiting list; a survey determines which upgrades are suitable for your home

procedure_steps.detail: Apply online or by phone to SEAI with details of your qualifying payment and your MPRN
SEAI arranges a home survey and recommends suitable measures
An SEAI-appointed contractor carries out the works free of charge

documents_required.doc: Proof of qualifying social welfare payment
MPRN and details of the property

eligibility.income_note: No income test; you must own and live in the home, it must have been built before 2006, you must receive an eligible social welfare payment, and a home survey must show it is suitable for upgrades.

programmes.source_snippet: From March 2026, those on qualifying welfare payments (including Fuel Allowance) also receive enhanced individual grants: a flat €2,500 for attic insulation and €2,300 for cavity wall insulation; the Warmer Homes Scheme itself is completely free

programmes.amount_note: EUR38 per week (2026) during the fuel season (late September to April, 28 weeks); only one payment per household
programmes.deadline_note: Apply before the start of the fuel season in September; claims are not backdated

procedure_steps.detail: Apply online via MyWelfare or with form NFS1 before the season starts
DSP checks you receive a qualifying payment or pass the means test (aged 66+, on long-term payments, or Working Family Payment recipients from 2026)

documents_required.doc: Details of household composition and heating costs

eligibility.income_note: Means test for aged 66+: weekly means up to EUR534 single = EUR27,768/yr (value shown, 534 x 52); EUR1,068/wk couple = EUR55,536/yr; first EUR50,000 of capital disregarded. Under 66 you must get a qualifying social welfare payment and means must not exceed the max State Pension (Contributory) plus EUR200 (about EUR499.30 single, 2026); first EUR20,000 of capital disregarded. You must live in Ireland and live alone or only with certain people.

programmes.source_snippet: The weekly rate increased to €38 in January 2026 (up from €33), and the scheme was also expanded to include Working Family Payment recipients

programmes.amount_note: EUR1.15 per day (about EUR34.50 a month) Electricity or Gas Allowance (you choose one) plus a free TV licence; everyone aged 70+ qualifies regardless of income; some people aged 66-70 qualify on a means test or qualifying payment; one Package per household

procedure_steps.detail: Apply online via MyWelfare or with form HB1
DSP checks age, residence and (if under 70) your qualifying payment or means

eligibility.income_note: No fixed euro ceiling is published. Aged 70+ there is no means test. Aged 66-70 without a qualifying payment, weekly means must not exceed the maximum State Pension (Contributory) plus EUR200 a week, so it moves with the pension rate. You can rent a room earning up to EUR269.23 a week without affecting the Package.

programmes.source_snippet: The Household Benefits Package includes the Electricity or Gas Allowance and Free TV Licence. If you are aged 70 or over, you qualify regardless of your income or who lives with you.

programmes.amount_note: Free travel on all State public transport (Bus Éireann, Dublin Bus, Iarnród Éireann, Luas, DART) and many private bus and ferry services for everyone aged 66+ permanently living in Ireland, and for certain people under 66 with disabilities or on carer's payments

procedure_steps.detail: Free Travel is normally issued automatically with your Public Services Card when you turn 66 or start a qualifying payment
If not automatic, apply via MyWelfare or your Intreo Centre

eligibility.income_note: Not means-tested at 66+; under 66 you qualify on certain disability or carer's payments

programmes.source_snippet: Everyone aged 66 and over, living permanently in Ireland, qualifies for the Free Travel Scheme.

programmes.name_en: TFI Young Adult / Student Leap Card (50% fares)
programmes.funder: National Transport Authority (NTA) / TFI Leap Card
programmes.amount_note: 50% discount on TFI public transport fares (Dublin Bus, Bus Éireann, Iarnród Éireann, Luas, Go-Ahead Ireland, TFI Local Link) for 19-25 year olds (Young Adult Card) and eligible students (Student Leap Card); daily and weekly fare capping applies

procedure_steps.detail: Order a Young Adult Leap Card (age 19-25) or Student Leap Card online at leapcard.ie with a photo and proof of age/student status
Top up the card and tag on; discounted fares and capping apply automatically

documents_required.doc: Proof of age (19-25) or valid student ID

programmes.source_snippet: Young Adult (19-25) and Student Leap Card holders get 50% off TFI fares, subject to daily and weekly fare caps

programmes.name_local: Cycle to Work Scheme (Scéim Rothar go dtí an Obair)
programmes.amount_note: Tax-free benefit (exempt from Income Tax, USC and PRSI) up to €1,250 for a bicycle and safety equipment, €1,500 for an e-bike, and €3,000 for a cargo/ecargo bike, claimed once every 4 years via salary sacrifice
programmes.deadline_note: Can be used once every 4 years

procedure_steps.detail: Check that your employer operates the scheme
Choose a bicycle and safety equipment from a supplier; your employer pays the supplier directly or via a voucher
The cost is recovered from your gross salary over up to 12 months before tax is calculated

documents_required.doc: Invoice for the bicycle and safety equipment made out to your employer

programmes.source_snippet: The current limits set by Revenue are €1,250 for a standard bicycle, €1,500 for an electric bicycle (e-bike), and €3,000 for an e-cargo bicycle; safety equipment is included within these limits; specifically exempt from benefit-in-kind (BIK) tax

programmes.funder: Revenue Commissioners (operated via employers and public transport operators)
programmes.amount_note: Employees save Income Tax, USC and PRSI on the cost of commuter tickets bought through their employer by salary deduction - typically 27.2%-52.2% off the normal price depending on ticket type and your tax rate

procedure_steps.detail: Ask your employer to register for the TaxSaver scheme on taxsaver.ie
Order your monthly or annual ticket; the cost is deducted from your gross salary before tax

documents_required.doc: Employer registration with the TaxSaver scheme

programmes.source_snippet: TaxSaver commuter tickets give employees tax savings on annual and monthly bus and rail tickets purchased through their employer

programmes.funder: Student Universal Support Ireland (SUSI, a business unit of CDETB)
programmes.amount_note: Maintenance grant paid monthly for 9 months: 2026/27 rates — special rate €7,936 (non-adjacent) / €3,230 (adjacent); full maintenance €4,722/€1,774; part-maintenance bands down to €1,866/€612; fee grant pays all or part of the student contribution and tuition
programmes.deadline_note: 2026/27 priority closing dates (11 June 2026 renewing, 9 July 2026 new applicants) have passed; late applications are still accepted - the final closing date is usually in November. Applications for the following year open in spring

procedure_steps.detail: Use the Eligibility Reckoner on susi.ie to check your means and nationality/residence criteria
Create a SUSI account and submit your application online
Upload supporting income documents when requested; SUSI assesses and issues a decision

documents_required.doc: PPS numbers for applicant and relevant family members
Proof of reckonable income (e.g. Revenue documents, social welfare statements)
Proof of residence and course acceptance

eligibility.income_note: Reckonable household income (2026/27, <4 dependent children): special rate <EUR28,600; full maintenance (Band 1) <EUR47,010; part maintenance bands up to <EUR58,470; 50% tuition+100% contribution <EUR64,315; EUR500 contribution grant up to <EUR120,000 (value shown = highest threshold for any SUSI support). Thresholds rise with dependent children (+EUR4,950 per additional person). Holiday earnings disregard EUR8,830.

programmes.source_snippet: Rates for the Student Grant Scheme 2026-2027: Special rate €7,936 non-adjacent / €3,230 adjacent; Full maintenance Band 1 €4,722 / €1,774

programmes.funder: Department of Further and Higher Education, Research, Innovation and Science
programmes.amount_note: The State pays tuition fees to the college for eligible full-time undergraduates; you still pay the annual student contribution (maximum EUR2,500) unless covered by a SUSI fee grant

procedure_steps.detail: Apply for your course through the CAO (or direct entry); the college claims the tuition fee from the Department for eligible students
Pay the student contribution charge at registration (or have it covered by a SUSI grant)

documents_required.doc: Course registration with an approved publicly funded institution

eligibility.income_note: Not means-tested for tuition; you must be a first-time undergraduate, EU/EEA/Swiss national or meet residence criteria, on an approved full-time course

programmes.source_snippet: Most undergraduate students attending publicly funded third-level courses do not have to pay tuition fees. The Free Fees Initiative means the Department pays the fees to the colleges instead.

programmes.name_local: Student Assistance Fund (Cúnamh do Mhic Léinn)
programmes.funder: Higher Education Authority (HEA), administered by colleges
programmes.amount_note: Financial support for registered full-time or part-time higher education students who experience financial difficulty — for books, class materials, rent, heating, food, essential travel and childcare; amount set by each institution
programmes.deadline_note: Application windows are set by each college, usually once or twice per semester

procedure_steps.detail: Contact the access or student services office in your college for the SAF application form
Provide evidence of income and the costs you cannot meet

documents_required.doc: Proof of income (social welfare, payslips, SUSI award)
Evidence of costs claimed (receipts, rent agreement)

eligibility.income_note: Targeted at students in financial need; you must be registered on a course of at least one year leading to a recognised qualification

programmes.source_snippet: The Student Assistance Fund provides financial assistance to full-time or part-time higher education students experiencing financial difficulties while attending college

programmes.funder: Department of Further and Higher Education (administered by participating higher education institutions)
programmes.amount_note: €5,000 per year for each year of undergraduate study for students from groups under-represented in higher education (e.g. socio-economically disadvantaged, lone parents, ethnic minorities, students with disabilities), awarded through participating colleges
programmes.deadline_note: Applications are made in autumn of first year through your college's access office

procedure_steps.detail: Enter a participating college through the CAO (often via HEAR/DARE or an access route)
Apply for the 1916 Bursary through your college's access office in first year, with evidence of income and circumstances

eligibility.income_note: For socio-economically disadvantaged students; income criterion is the SUSI special rate threshold (reckonable income < EUR28,600, 2026/27) plus other disadvantage indicators.

programmes.source_snippet: The 1916 Bursary provides €5,000 per year of study to students who are socio-economically disadvantaged and from groups most under-represented in higher education

programmes.funder: Higher Education Authority (HEA) / Department of Further and Higher Education
programmes.amount_note: Free part-time higher education courses for unemployed people and returners to the workforce; people in employment typically pay 10% of the course fee (level 6 fully funded; micro-credential courses funded at 50%)
programmes.deadline_note: Courses open for applications from around May-June each year for autumn start

procedure_steps.detail: Browse approved courses on springboardcourses.ie and apply directly to the college
Provide evidence of your employment status (unemployed applicants get 100% funding; employed pay 10%)

documents_required.doc: Proof of employment status (e.g. DSP payment or payslips)
Academic transcripts / evidence of prior learning

eligibility.income_note: Not means-tested; level of subsidy depends on employment status (free for jobseekers and homemakers/returners; 90% for those in employment)

programmes.source_snippet: Springboard+ provides free higher education courses for people who are unemployed and 90% funded courses for people in employment, in areas of identified skills need

programmes.funder: Department of Education (operated by Bus Éireann)
programmes.amount_note: Subsidised bus transport for eligible primary pupils living 3.2km+ and post-primary pupils living 4.8km+ from their nearest school; annual ticket fee capped per family, free for children with medical cards; Remote Area Grants support families not served by a route
programmes.deadline_note: Applications and payments must be made before the deadline for the school year (usually in spring/summer)

procedure_steps.detail: Apply or pay online via the Bus Éireann School Transport portal before the deadline
Bus Éireann assesses eligibility based on distance to the nearest suitable school

documents_required.doc: Child's PPS number and school details

programmes.source_snippet: School Transport is a significant operation managed by Bus Éireann on behalf of the Department of Education, providing transport for eligible children to their nearest school

programmes.name_local: HEAR and DARE College Access Schemes
programmes.amount_note: Reduced-points college places and post-entry supports: HEAR for school leavers from socio-economically disadvantaged backgrounds; DARE for school leavers with disabilities; applied for through the CAO
programmes.deadline_note: Apply to the CAO by 5pm on 1 February; complete the HEAR/DARE application by 5pm on 1 March (DARE applicants must be under 23 on 1 January of the entry year); dates repeat each year

procedure_steps.detail: Apply to the CAO and tick the HEAR and/or DARE box
Complete the online HEAR/DARE application form with income (HEAR) or disability (DARE) evidence
If eligible, you compete for reserved reduced-points places at participating colleges

eligibility.income_note: HEAR uses income, means and socio-economic indicators; DARE uses evidence of disability impact on education

programmes.source_snippet: HEAR (Higher Education Access Route) and DARE (Disability Access Route to Education) are third-level alternative admissions schemes for school-leavers whose socio-economic background or disability has negatively impacted their education

programmes.name_local: Back to Education Allowance (Liúntas um Fhilleadh ar an Oideachas)
programmes.amount_note: Weekly payment at the same rate as your qualifying social welfare payment (plus any qualified-adult/child increases) while you study; an annual Cost of Education Allowance of EUR500 applies if you have a dependent child
programmes.deadline_note: You must apply before starting (or within 30 days of starting) the course

procedure_steps.detail: Get accepted on an approved course at a recognised school or college
Apply via MyWelfare or at your Intreo Centre; you must have been on a qualifying social welfare payment for the required period (3-12 months depending on the course level)

documents_required.doc: Details of your qualifying social welfare payment

eligibility.income_note: You must have been getting a qualifying social welfare payment for a minimum period before the course; you cannot get BTEA and a full SUSI maintenance grant together

programmes.source_snippet: The Back to Education Allowance lets people on certain social welfare payments keep a payment while studying an approved full-time second-level or third-level course

programmes.funder: Department of Social Protection (DSP) / local CE sponsoring organisations
programmes.amount_note: Part-time (19.5 hours/week) paid work placements in local community projects; minimum weekly payment for new participants is EUR286.50 (2026), or your social welfare rate plus EUR32.50 if higher; usually 1 year

procedure_steps.detail: Register your interest with your local Intreo Centre or apply directly to a CE scheme sponsor advertising vacancies (e.g. on JobsIreland.ie)
Eligibility: generally aged 21+ and 12 months or more on a qualifying social welfare payment (shorter for some groups)

documents_required.doc: Details of your social welfare payment history

eligibility.income_note: You must be in receipt of a qualifying social welfare payment (e.g. Jobseeker's Allowance) for at least 12 months (6 months for some categories)

programmes.source_snippet: Community Employment helps people get back to work by offering part-time and temporary placements in jobs based within local communities

programmes.funder: Department of Social Protection (DSP) / Local Development Companies
programmes.amount_note: 12-month, 19.5-hours-per-week work placements in community and voluntary organisations; minimum weekly payment EUR286.50 (2026), or your Jobseeker's Allowance rate plus EUR32.50 if higher
programmes.deadline_note: Participants are selected by random contact from the live register; you can also self-refer through your Intreo Centre

procedure_steps.detail: Be contacted by the DSP (random selection) or express interest at your Intreo Centre
Interview with the local development company running Tús in your area and start your 12-month placement

documents_required.doc: Proof of 12 months on Jobseeker's Allowance

eligibility.income_note: You must be fully unemployed and in receipt of Jobseeker's Allowance for at least 12 months

programmes.source_snippet: Tús provides short-term, quality work opportunities for people who are unemployed for more than a year, in community and voluntary organisations

programmes.amount_note: Incentive paid to employers monthly in arrears over 18 months: EUR7,500 for recruiting someone on a qualifying payment (Jobseeker, Disability Allowance or Blind Pension) for 12 of the previous 18 months; EUR10,000 if the employee is over 50 or has been on a qualifying payment for 24 of the previous 30 months

procedure_steps.detail: Employer registers a vacancy on JobsIreland.ie and applies for JobsPlus before making the job offer
DSP confirms the candidate's eligibility and the grant is paid monthly in arrears to the employer

documents_required.doc: Details of the vacancy and the employee's unemployment record

eligibility.income_note: Employee must be unemployed and in receipt of a qualifying payment; job must be at least 30 hours per week

programmes.source_snippet: JobsPlus provides a direct monthly payment to employers who recruit people from the live register: €7,500 over two years for those unemployed 12 months or more, €10,000 for those unemployed 24 months or more

programmes.amount_note: EUR369 per week for a 6-month, 30-hours-per-week work experience placement for people aged 18-65 on a qualifying social welfare payment for 4 months (under 30) or 6 months (over 30); no cost to the host employer

procedure_steps.detail: Apply for advertised WPEP placements through JobsIreland.ie or your Intreo case officer
The host organisation confirms the placement with the DSP; you are paid weekly by the DSP

documents_required.doc: Details of your qualifying social welfare payment

eligibility.income_note: You must be getting a qualifying social welfare payment and be unemployed for at least 6 months (some payments qualify regardless of duration)

programmes.source_snippet: WPEP gives people who have never had a job or who have lost their job the opportunity to get quality work experience for 6 months while keeping a weekly payment

programmes.name_local: Back to Work Enterprise Allowance (Liúntas Fiontair um Fhilleadh ar an Obair)
programmes.amount_note: Paid at 100% of your weekly social welfare rate in year 1 and 75% in year 2 while you set up as self-employed; for people on Jobseeker's Benefit/Allowance (or certain other payments) continuously for at least 9 months with a business plan approved in advance
programmes.deadline_note: You must apply before starting self-employment and have your business plan assessed

procedure_steps.detail: Develop your business idea and plan (Local Development Companies run Enterprise Supports)
Apply at your Intreo Centre before starting self-employment; a case officer reviews your plan

documents_required.doc: Details of your qualifying social welfare payment

eligibility.income_note: You must have been getting Jobseeker's Benefit or Allowance for at least 12 months (9 months for JB); the allowance ends if you take up employment

programmes.source_snippet: The Back to Work Enterprise Allowance encourages people getting certain social welfare payments to become self-employed by keeping a portion of their payment while their business is being established

programmes.amount_note: Weekly payment at your Jobseeker's Benefit rate while you start your own business, paid for the remainder of your JB entitlement (up to 9 months); for people who qualified for JB and became self-employed
programmes.deadline_note: Apply before starting self-employment

procedure_steps.detail: Apply at your Intreo Centre with form STEA1 and your business plan
A DSP case officer assesses the viability of the business

eligibility.income_note: You must be entitled to Jobseeker's Benefit; no means test on initial business income while on the allowance

programmes.source_snippet: The Short-Term Enterprise Allowance supports people who have lost their job and qualify for Jobseeker's Benefit to start their own business while keeping their payment

programmes.name_en: Skills to Advance (employee upskilling via ETBs)
programmes.funder: SOLAS and Education and Training Boards (ETBs)
programmes.amount_note: Free or heavily subsidised upskilling and reskilling courses for employees, especially those in lower-skilled jobs or vulnerable sectors, delivered by ETBs (day, evening and online options)

procedure_steps.detail: Browse courses or contact your local ETB's Skills to Advance team
Enrol on a suitable course; employers can also arrange subsidised training for staff

programmes.source_snippet: Skills to Advance offers upskilling and reskilling opportunities to employees in jobs undergoing change and to those currently employed in vulnerable sectors, at low or no cost

programmes.amount_note: Up to €1,000 per year for a single person or €2,000 for a jointly assessed couple, capped at 20% of rent paid; for tenants in RTB-registered private rented homes, rent-a-room or digs for work, or student accommodation
programmes.deadline_note: Claims can be made for the current year and backdated up to 4 years (2022 onwards)

procedure_steps.detail: Log in to Revenue myAccount and select 'Review your Tax' for the relevant year
Add the Rent Tax Credit, entering your RTB registration number and rent paid
Refunds are paid to your bank account, typically within weeks

eligibility.income_note: Not means-tested; you cannot claim if you get HAP, Rent Supplement or other State housing support, or rent from a parent/child or social landlord

programmes.source_snippet: The Rent Tax Credit is €1,000 per year for single tenants and €2,000 for married/civil partners (2024-2025 rates); requires RTB-registered tenancy as principal private residence

programmes.amount_note: Temporary credit on the increase in mortgage interest paid since 2022, for homeowners with an outstanding mortgage of €80,000-€500,000 at end-2022; maximum €1,250 for 2025 and a reduced maximum of €625 for 2026 (extended to 31 December 2026 on a tapered basis)
programmes.deadline_note: The 2025 credit (max €1,250) is claimed from 2026; the 2026 credit (max €625) from 2027

procedure_steps.detail: Get your certificate of mortgage interest from your lender for the relevant year and 2022
Claim through Revenue myAccount (Review your Tax) or your income tax return

documents_required.doc: Mortgage interest certificate from your lender
Proof of outstanding mortgage balance at 31 December 2022

programmes.source_snippet: The Finance Bill extends Mortgage Interest Tax Relief, on a tapered basis, for two further years, to 31 December 2026... maximum tax credit of €1,250 per property available to claim from 2026... a maximum tax credit of €625 per property available to claim from 2027

programmes.name_local: Home Carer Tax Credit (Creidmheas Cánach Cúramóra Baile)
programmes.amount_note: EUR1,950 per year (as previously recorded) for married/civil-partner couples jointly assessed where one partner cares at home for a dependent person; full credit if the carer's income is under EUR7,200, reduced above that, nil at EUR11,100 or more (2026)
programmes.deadline_note: Claim for the current year or backdate up to 4 years

procedure_steps.detail: Claim through Revenue myAccount under 'Add new tax credit' or on your Form 11/12
Provide details of the person cared for and the home carer's income

documents_required.doc: Details of the dependant being cared for

eligibility.income_note: The income test applies to the home carer's OWN income (not household): full EUR1,950 credit if income <= EUR7,200; reduced by EUR1 for every EUR2 above EUR7,200; nil at EUR11,100 (value shown). Couple must be married/civil partners and jointly assessed.

programmes.source_snippet: The Home Carer Tax Credit is €1,950 for couples taxed under joint assessment where one spouse or civil partner works in the home caring for a dependant

programmes.amount_note: €1,900 annual tax credit plus a €4,000 increase to your standard rate cut-off point, for a single parent (or primary claimant) with a qualifying child; only one claimant per child
programmes.deadline_note: Claim for the current year or backdate up to 4 years

procedure_steps.detail: Claim via Revenue myAccount ('Add new tax credit') or on your tax return
Confirm you are the child's primary carer and not cohabiting/married or jointly assessed

documents_required.doc: PPS number for you and the child

eligibility.income_note: You must not be living with a partner, married or in a civil partnership; the child must live with you for the whole or greater part of the year

programmes.source_snippet: The Single Person Child Carer Credit is €1,900, and the primary claimant is also entitled to an increase of €4,000 in the standard rate band

programmes.amount_note: €3,800 per year (2025/2026) per incapacitated child, for parents or guardians of a child who is permanently incapacitated (physically or mentally) from maintaining themselves
programmes.deadline_note: Claim for the current year or backdate up to 4 years

procedure_steps.detail: Claim via Revenue myAccount or your tax return
Provide a medical certificate confirming the nature and permanence of the child's incapacity (first claim only)

programmes.source_snippet: The Incapacitated Child Tax Credit is €3,800 for each incapacitated child, where the child is permanently incapacitated from maintaining themselves

programmes.amount_note: €305 per year (2025/2026) for maintaining a dependent relative at your own expense (e.g. widowed father or mother, elderly or incapacitated relative); the relative's income must not exceed the specified limit

procedure_steps.detail: Claim via Revenue myAccount or your tax return, giving the relative's details and income

documents_required.doc: Relative's PPS number and income details

eligibility.income_note: The dependent relative's own income must not exceed EUR18,548 (2026; EUR18,028 for 2025) for the credit to apply; all of the relative's income including social welfare and pensions counts.

programmes.source_snippet: You may claim the Dependent Relative Tax Credit if you maintain at your own expense a dependent relative such as a widowed parent or an incapacitated relative

programmes.amount_note: €245 per year for each person aged 65 or over (€490 for a married couple or civil partners, jointly assessed, where either is 65+)

procedure_steps.detail: Claim through Revenue myAccount when you or your spouse/partner turns 65

programmes.source_snippet: The Age Tax Credit is €245 for a single person aged 65 or over and €490 for a married couple or civil partners (jointly assessed) where either partner is 65 or over

programmes.amount_note: €1,950 per year if you are blind (€3,900 where both spouses/civil partners are blind), plus a further Blind Person's Guide Dog Allowance (€825 at 20% = €165) if you have a trained guide dog
programmes.deadline_note: Claim for the current year or backdate up to 4 years

procedure_steps.detail: Claim via Revenue myAccount with a certificate from an ophthalmic surgeon confirming your visual impairment

documents_required.doc: Guide dog certificate (if claiming the guide dog allowance)

programmes.source_snippet: The Blind Person's Tax Credit is €1,950; where both spouses or civil partners are blind the credit is €3,900

programmes.amount_note: Gross rental income from letting a room (or rooms) in your own home is exempt from Income Tax, USC and PRSI up to €14,000 per year; income above the limit is taxed in full

procedure_steps.detail: Let a room in your sole or main residence; if gross annual rental income stays under €14,000 the relief applies automatically (opt out on your tax return if preferred)

programmes.source_snippet: If you rent out a room in your home, rental income up to €14,000 per year is exempt from Income Tax, USC and PRSI under Rent-a-Room Relief

programmes.amount_note: Tax relief at your highest rate on 30% of the cost of electricity, heating and broadband for the days you work from home; alternatively your employer can pay €3.20 per day tax-free
programmes.deadline_note: Claim after the end of the tax year (backdate up to 4 years); employer daily payments are made through payroll

procedure_steps.detail: Keep utility bills and record the number of days worked from home
Claim through Revenue myAccount at year end ('Add tax credits' > 'Remote Working Relief') or ask your employer to pay the €3.20/day tax-free allowance

documents_required.doc: Record of days worked from home

programmes.source_snippet: If your employer does not make a payment of €3.20 per day, or pays you less than your allowable costs, you can claim Remote Working Relief. The relief is given at your highest rate of tax.

programmes.amount_note: Employers can give an employee up to five qualifying non-cash incentives per tax year tax-free, with a cumulative annual value not exceeding €1,500 (from 1 January 2025); employer reports each benefit to Revenue in real time
programmes.deadline_note: Maximum of two benefits per calendar year; any unused amount cannot be carried forward

procedure_steps.detail: Your employer provides the voucher or non-cash benefit and reports it to Revenue through Enhanced Reporting Requirements (ERR)

documents_required.doc: Employer payroll / ERR report of the benefit

programmes.source_snippet: From 1 January 2025, employers can provide up to five qualifying incentives to an employee in any tax year, with a cumulative annual value not exceeding €1,500.

programmes.amount_note: Tax relief at 20% on qualifying health expenses you paid for yourself or others: GP and consultant fees, prescriptions (net of Drugs Payment Scheme cap), physiotherapy, non-routine dental treatment and nursing home costs (relief at 40% for nursing home fees)
programmes.deadline_note: Claim after the end of the tax year; you can backdate claims up to 4 years

procedure_steps.detail: Keep receipts for qualifying medical expenses
Claim through Revenue myAccount (Health Expenses) at the end of the year

documents_required.doc: Receipts for all qualifying health expenses

programmes.source_snippet: You generally receive tax relief at your standard rate of 20%. Nursing home expenses are given at your highest rate of tax (up to 40%). The four-year rule applies.

programmes.name_local: Trading Online Voucher Scheme (Deontas Trádála Ar Líne)
programmes.funder: Local Enterprise Offices (Department of Enterprise, Trade and Employment)
programmes.amount_note: Voucher of up to €2,500 with 50% matched funding from the business, to develop an e-commerce website, online payments/booking systems, apps or digital marketing; a second voucher may be available
programmes.deadline_note: Do not start the work before approval; a free online information session is usually required first

procedure_steps.detail: Attend your LEO's free Trading Online information session
Get quotes from your web/digital provider and submit the application form to your Local Enterprise Office
After approval and completion of the works, submit invoices for reimbursement of 50% up to €2,500

documents_required.doc: Written quote(s) for the digital works

eligibility.income_note: Business must have 10 or fewer employees, turnover under €2 million, at least 6 months trading, and limited or no e-commerce presence

programmes.source_snippet: Trading Online Voucher Scheme. This scheme is a matched-funding opportunity with up to €2,500 available

programmes.amount_note: Normally up to 50% of investment, up to €80,000 (up to €150,000 in certain situations); start-ups within first 18 months, up to 10 employees

procedure_steps.detail: Discuss your business plan with your Local Enterprise Office before applying
Submit the grant application with business plan, quotes and financial projections
Grants are paid on evidence of expenditure; jobs must be created within the agreed period

eligibility.income_note: For manufacturing or internationally traded services businesses in the commercial sphere, in their first 18 months, employing up to 10 people

programmes.source_snippet: up to €80,000 ... up to €150,000 in certain situations ... not exceed 50% of the investment ... within the first 18 months of start-up

programmes.amount_note: Up to 50% of investment, maximum €150,000 or whichever is the lesser; for micro-enterprises with up to 10 employees after the initial 18-month start-up period

procedure_steps.detail: Contact your LEO to discuss the expansion project before applying
Submit application with business plan, quotes and employment projections

eligibility.income_note: Business must be trading for at least 18 months with up to 10 employees, in manufacturing or internationally traded services

programmes.source_snippet: employing up to 10 staff in its growth phase after the initial 18-month start-up period ... €150,000 - or whichever is the lesser ... not exceed 50% of the investment

programmes.amount_note: From 50% (South and East Region) to 60% (Border Midlands West Region) of investment, up to a maximum of €15,000

procedure_steps.detail: Discuss your proposed study with your LEO
Apply with a description of the business idea and quotes for the research work

documents_required.doc: Description of the business idea and study scope

programmes.source_snippet: from 50% (in the South and East Region) to 60% (in the Borders Midlands, West Region) of investment ... up to a maximum of €15,000, whichever is the lesser

programmes.name_en: New Frontiers Entrepreneur Development Programme (Enterprise Ireland)
programmes.funder: Enterprise Ireland (delivered by Technological Universities and Universities)
programmes.amount_note: Support package worth over €30,000 with no equity taken; includes training, mentoring and a stipend. Application deadlines per programme location are listed on the calendar page
programmes.deadline_note: Programme phases run several times a year at partner campuses nationwide

procedure_steps.detail: Apply online to the New Frontiers programme at your nearest partner institution
Complete Phase 1 (part-time validation) then compete for a place on the 6-month full-time Phase 2 with stipend

documents_required.doc: Business idea outline and application form
Commitment to work full-time on the venture during Phase 2

programmes.source_snippet: New Frontiers is ideal for first-time founders who want to build their startup toolkit, learn about the Irish startup ecosystem, and grow their professional network.

programmes.amount_note: Investment of up to €50,000 for a 10% equity stake in early-stage startups with high growth and export potential; periodic sector-specific calls (e.g. women entrepreneurs, all sectors)
programmes.deadline_note: Runs in calls with fixed deadlines published on enterprise-ireland.com

procedure_steps.detail: Check the current CSF call and eligibility on enterprise-ireland.com
Submit the online application with business plan and pitch video before the call deadline
Successful applicants negotiate the equity investment agreement with Enterprise Ireland

documents_required.doc: Online application and executive business summary

programmes.source_snippet: The Competitive Start Fund accelerates the growth of early-stage startup companies with the potential to grow in international markets, offering up to €50,000 in equity funding

programmes.funder: Local Action Groups (Department of Rural and Community Development, EU co-funded)
programmes.amount_note: EU co-funded grants for rural enterprises, community groups and farmers: typically up to 50-75% of project costs (higher rates for community projects), for enterprise development, rural tourism, broadband and community infrastructure
programmes.deadline_note: Calls and themes are set by each Local Action Group under its Local Development Strategy

procedure_steps.detail: Contact the Local Development Company (Local Action Group) covering your area
Complete an Expression of Interest and, if invited, a full application with project costs and business plan

eligibility.income_note: Projects must be in rural areas (outside the main cities and large towns); grant rate depends on project type and promoter

programmes.source_snippet: Prospective applicants should contact their LAG through its Implementing Partner (where applicable) to register an expression of interest and discuss the eligibility of a project proposal

programmes.amount_note: Employers must pay 70% of your normal daily pay, up to a maximum of €110 per day, for 5 sick days per year (2026); Illness Benefit may be payable for further days
programmes.deadline_note: 5 statutory sick days per calendar year; unused days do not carry over

procedure_steps.detail: Give your employer a medical certificate for the days you are sick
Your employer pays statutory sick pay through payroll for up to 5 days a year

documents_required.doc: Medical certificate for sick days claimed

eligibility.income_note: You must have worked for your employer for at least 13 continuous weeks

programmes.source_snippet: Workers will be entitled to up to 5 days of sick leave in a year, paid at 70% of gross earning, up to a cap of €110.

programmes.name_local: Living Alone Increase (Méadú do Dhaoine ina gCónaí ina nAonar)
programmes.amount_note: €22 per week (2026) extra on your social welfare pension or certain other payments if you live alone; automatic for people getting a pension at 66+ who live alone

procedure_steps.detail: If you are 66 or over and get a social welfare pension, the increase is usually added automatically when you confirm you live alone
Under 66 on certain payments: complete the declaration on your application or contact the DSP

eligibility.income_note: Not means-tested; paid with a qualifying social welfare payment if you live alone

programmes.source_snippet: If you are aged 66 or over and live alone, you will qualify for the Living Alone Increase if you are getting one of the following payments: State Pension (Contributory)...

programmes.amount_note: €2.50 per week extra (2026) for people on certain social welfare payments who are living alone and also get the Living Alone Increase and Fuel Allowance (helps with phone or personal alarm costs)

procedure_steps.detail: Paid automatically if you qualify for both the Living Alone Increase and Fuel Allowance

documents_required.doc: No application needed if on qualifying payments

eligibility.income_note: Paid with qualifying social welfare payments to people living alone

programmes.source_snippet: Telephone Support Allowance €2.50 weekly; you must be getting both the Living Alone Increase and the Fuel Allowance

programmes.name_local: Scéim um Chúram agus Oideachas na Luath-Óige (ECCE)
programmes.name_en: Early Childhood Care and Education (ECCE) free pre-school programme
programmes.funder: Department of Children, Disability and Equality (DCDE)
programmes.amount_note: Free pre-school: 3 hours a day, 5 days a week, 38 weeks a year (15 free hours per week) for up to 2 programme years; DCDE pays the provider directly. Extra hours are charged by the provider but may be subsidised by the National Childcare Scheme
programmes.deadline_note: Single enrolment point each September; apply directly to a participating pre-school provider

procedure_steps.detail: Check your child's eligibility by birth date (children can start from age 2 years 8 months, until they start primary school, max age 5 years 6 months at end of June)
Enrol your child with a participating ECCE-registered pre-school provider

documents_required.doc: Child's proof of date of birth and PPS number

eligibility.income_note: Not means-tested; universal free entitlement for children aged 2 years 8 months to 5 years 6 months

programmes.source_snippet: The ECCE scheme provides up to 2 years of early childhood care and education for children of pre-school age.

programmes.funder: Department of Children, Disability and Equality (administered by Pobal)
programmes.amount_note: Universal subsidy €2.14 per hour per child, up to 45 hours/week for enhanced; income-assessed subsidy up to €5.10 an hour depending on income

procedure_steps.detail: Apply online at ncs.gov.ie with a verified MyGovID (or by post via the NCS Parent Support Centre)
Receive a CHICK code and give it to your childcare provider to register the claim
Subsidy is paid to the provider and subtracted from your bill; renew each programme year

documents_required.doc: PPS numbers and dates of birth for children (and partner)

eligibility.income_note: Universal subsidy not means-tested. Income-assessed subsidy: maximum rate up to income threshold €34,000, tapering to cut-off threshold €68,000 (annual reckonable household income)

programmes.source_snippet: Aged between 6 months (24 weeks) and 15 years (children aged 15 do not qualify)

programmes.name_local: Dibhinn Filleadh ar Obair do Theaghlaigh (BTWFD)
programmes.amount_note: From January 2026: year 1 €58/week per child under 12 and €78/week per child 12+; year 2 €29 and €39 per week respectively

procedure_steps.detail: Take up employment/self-employment in Ireland within 4 weeks of leaving your jobseeker's or One-Parent Family payment (at least 12 months on payment, 6 in the last year)
All family members sign off primary social welfare payments; apply via MyWelfare or your Intreo centre

eligibility.income_note: No income test - BTWFD is paid regardless of earnings; you cannot combine it with a primary social welfare payment but it can be paid with Working Family Payment

programmes.source_snippet: From January 2026, the full BTWFD is €58 for a child aged under 12 and €78 for a child aged 12 and over. In the second year, it is reduced to €29 for a child aged under 12 and €39 for a child aged 12 and over.

programmes.amount_note: EUR237 per week (2026) for a person caring for an orphan (child under 18, or 22 in full-time education, whose parents are dead, unknown or have abandoned them). Contributory version is based on a parent's PRSI and is not means-tested; non-contributory version is means-tested on the orphan's own means

procedure_steps.detail: Get a Guardian's Payment application form (GP1) from your local post office or Intreo centre
Send the completed form to Guardian's Payment Section, DSP, College Road, Sligo

documents_required.doc: Child's birth certificate and PPS number
Death certificate(s) of parent(s) or evidence of abandonment

eligibility.income_note: Contributory payment: no means test (needs 26 weeks PRSI by a parent/step-parent). Non-contributory: means test on the ORPHAN's own means only (first EUR7.60/wk disregarded); guardian's income is not assessed.

programmes.source_snippet: In 2026, the Guardian's Payment (Contributory) is paid at a standard rate of €237 per week and the maximum Guardian's Payment (Non-Contributory) is €237 per week.

programmes.name_en: Bereaved Parent Grant (formerly Widowed or Surviving Civil Partner Grant)
programmes.amount_note: Once-off payment of EUR8,000 for a widow, widower, surviving civil partner or surviving cohabitant (deaths on/after 21 July 2025) with dependent children, who also qualifies for a payment such as the Bereaved Partner's Contributory Pension, One-Parent Family Payment, Death Benefit, or a State Pension

procedure_steps.detail: No separate form needed if you are applying for the Bereaved Partner's (Contributory) Pension or One-Parent Family Payment; otherwise complete form WPG1/BPG1
Send to the Bereaved Partner's Pension Section, DSP, College Road, Sligo

eligibility.income_note: Not means-tested; entitlement depends on qualifying for an underlying social welfare payment

programmes.source_snippet: The Bereaved Parent Grant is a once-off payment of €8,000.

programmes.amount_note: Free mammogram every 2 years for women aged 50 to 69; letter of invitation sent automatically to women registered with a GP / on the BreastCheck register

procedure_steps.detail: Check you are on the BreastCheck register (or register online/by phone) and wait for your invitation letter
Attend the appointment at a BreastCheck screening unit or mobile unit

eligibility.income_note: Not means-tested; free for all women in the eligible age range

programmes.source_snippet: Breast screening is for women and anyone age 50 to 69 with breasts or female breast tissue.

programmes.name_local: CervicalCheck - An Clár Náisiúnta Scagtha Ceirbheacs
programmes.amount_note: Free cervical screening test (HPV cervical screening) for women and people with a cervix aged 25 to 65; frequency depends on age and results (every 3 or 5 years)

procedure_steps.detail: Check the CervicalCheck register and book a free test with a registered GP practice, GP or nurse when your test is due

eligibility.income_note: Not means-tested; free for everyone with a cervix aged 25-65

programmes.source_snippet: Free cervical screening is for women and anyone age 25 to 65 with a cervix.

programmes.name_local: BowelScreen - An Clár Náisiúnta Scagtha Putóige
programmes.amount_note: Free home bowel screening test (FIT) kit every 2 years for people aged 59 to 69

procedure_steps.detail: Register with BowelScreen (freephone or online) if you have not received an invitation
Complete the home test kit and return it by Freepost

eligibility.income_note: Not means-tested; free for all aged 59-70

programmes.source_snippet: The eligible age range for bowel screening is now 59 to 69 (previously 60 to 69).

programmes.name_local: Vacsain fliú saor in aisce do ghrúpaí atá i mbaol
programmes.name_en: Free HSE Flu Vaccine for at-risk groups
programmes.amount_note: Free annual flu vaccine (October-April) for people aged 60+, pregnant women, children aged 2-17 (nasal vaccine), healthcare workers, and people with long-term medical conditions or weakened immune systems; available from GPs and pharmacies
programmes.deadline_note: Available from October to end of April each year

procedure_steps.detail: Contact your GP or participating pharmacy for a free flu vaccine if you are in an eligible group

eligibility.income_note: Not means-tested; free for the HSE-defined at-risk and age groups

programmes.source_snippet: You can get a free flu vaccine if you: are age 60 and older are age 2 to 17 are a healthcare worker are pregnant live in a nursing home or other long-term care

programmes.funder: Department of Social Protection / Education and Training Boards (ETBs)
programmes.amount_note: No fees; training allowance paid at the maximum rate of Jobseeker's Allowance (weekly); free books and materials may apply. Course up to 2 years
programmes.deadline_note: Courses generally start in September; apply through your local ETB VTOS centre

procedure_steps.detail: Confirm eligibility with your Intreo case officer (aged 21+ and 6 months/156 days on a qualifying social welfare payment)
Apply for a VTOS course at your local ETB centre or via fetchcourses.ie
Complete VTOS application with the college coordinator and your Intreo office

documents_required.doc: Evidence of qualifying social welfare payment (156 days)

eligibility.income_note: No separate income test; eligibility is based on receipt of a qualifying social welfare payment for at least 6 months (means-tested payments have their own income rules)

programmes.source_snippet: VTOS participants who move from jobseeker's payments get a VTOS training allowance at the maximum rate of the jobseeker's payment.

programmes.funder: Department of Education / Education and Training Boards (ETBs)
programmes.amount_note: One- to two-year further-education courses (QQI Level 5/6) with no tuition fees; a participant contribution of EUR200/year applies but is waived for full medical card holders (and their dependent children), student-grant holders, and BTEA/VTOS recipients; SUSI maintenance grants and Back to Education Allowance may be available
programmes.deadline_note: Apply to the college/ETB directly or via fetchcourses.ie before the academic year

procedure_steps.detail: Find a PLC course on fetchcourses.ie or Qualifax and apply to the college
Attend an informal interview if called; claim the EUR200 contribution waiver if eligible

documents_required.doc: Leaving Certificate or evidence of relevant experience
documents_required.note: mature applicants without Leaving Cert may be accepted

eligibility.income_note: No income test for the course itself; the EUR200 participant contribution is waived for full medical card holders, SUSI grantees and BTEA/VTOS recipients

programmes.source_snippet: You must pay a participant contribution fee of €200 per year to do a PLC course.

programmes.name_en: Erasmus+ student and staff mobility grant
programmes.amount_note: EU grant for higher-education students doing a study period or traineeship in another programme country; monthly grant amounts and top-ups (e.g. for students from disadvantaged backgrounds) are set annually by the higher-education institution and national agency Léargas; tuition fees at the host institution are waived
programmes.deadline_note: Apply through your college's international/Erasmus office before its internal deadline

procedure_steps.detail: Apply through the Erasmus/international office of your Irish higher-education institution
Sign a grant agreement; the grant is paid by your home institution during the mobility

documents_required.doc: Learning agreement approved by home and host institutions

eligibility.income_note: Base grant is not means-tested; additional top-ups target students from disadvantaged backgrounds

programmes.source_snippet: Erasmus+ supports study periods and traineeships abroad for higher education students, with a monthly mobility grant paid through the home institution.

programmes.amount_note: Weekly allowance replacing Jobseeker's Allowance for long-term jobseekers who take up part-time work under 24 hours/week: EUR160.90/week single or EUR262.40/week with a qualified adult (2026); paid regardless of part-time earnings; not taxable; initially for one year (extendable) while seeking full-time work

procedure_steps.detail: Be on long-term Jobseeker's Allowance (312+ days) with a weekly payment of at least EUR160.90 (single) or EUR262.40 (with qualified adult)
Get part-time work under 24 hrs/week (PRSI Class A or J, likely to last 2 months) and apply to your Intreo centre before starting

documents_required.doc: Details of the part-time job (employer, hours, PRSI class)

eligibility.income_note: No means test while on the scheme - the allowance is paid regardless of part-time earnings; entry requires a prior JA payment of at least EUR160.90/wk (single)

programmes.source_snippet: €160.90 per week if you are single; €262.40 per week if you are getting an increase for a qualified adult. On long-term Jobseeker's Allowance (JA) for at least 312 days.

programmes.name_en: Wage Subsidy Scheme (WSS) for people with disabilities
programmes.amount_note: From April 2026 per employee with a disability: €7.50/hour (1-6 subsidised employees), €8.50/hour (7-16), €10.00/hour (17+); maximum annual subsidy €15,210 based on a 39-hour week; employee must work at least 15 hours a week

procedure_steps.detail: Employer agrees terms with the DSP and the employee must be referred/approved (disability with 80% or less productivity)
Employer completes the online wage subsidy request on Welfare Partners every 4 weeks

documents_required.doc: Evidence of employee's disability and productivity assessment

eligibility.income_note: No income test on the employee; subsidy is based on the job and paid to the employer

programmes.source_snippet: The maximum annual subsidy to the employer is €15,210, based on a 39-hour week.

programmes.name_en: Work and Access Programme (DSP disability employment supports)
programmes.amount_note: Workplace Needs Assessment up to €2,500; In-Work Support up to €12,500 a year; Work Equipment up to €12,000; Workplace Adaptation up to €25,000; Disability Equality and Inclusion Training 80-90% of cost up to €20,000 over 12 months

procedure_steps.detail: Complete form WA1 (individual) or WA2 (employer) available from your Intreo office or gov.ie
Email to workandaccess@welfare.ie or post to DSP Work and Access Section; get approval BEFORE buying any support

documents_required.note: must be completed and recommend the supports

eligibility.income_note: No income test; supports are needs-based for people with a disability in or entering employment

programmes.source_snippet: Work and Access can pay up to €25,000 towards these changes.

programmes.funder: Microfinance Ireland (Microenterprise Loan Fund, Dept of Enterprise)
programmes.amount_note: Government-backed unsecured loans of EUR2,000 to EUR50,000 (limit doubled from EUR25,000 in 2024) for micro-enterprises (fewer than 10 employees, turnover under EUR2m) that struggle to get bank finance; terms 1-5 years, no fees; 1% interest-rate reduction when applying through a Local Enterprise Office

procedure_steps.detail: Prepare business plan and financials; apply online to Microfinance Ireland or via your Local Enterprise Office for the discounted rate

documents_required.doc: Bank statements / evidence of credit difficulty

eligibility.income_note: No income test; business must have fewer than 10 employees and annual turnover under EUR2 million

programmes.source_snippet: We provide business loans of €2,000 to €50,000

programmes.amount_note: Refund of Income Tax paid in previous years (up to 6 years back) for people leaving PAYE employment (or recently unemployed/redundant) who invest cash in shares of a new qualifying company and work in it full-time; refund depends on tax previously paid (worth up to roughly 40% of the investment); investment limits EUR250 minimum and EUR140,000 maximum per year of assessment (max EUR980,000 over 7 years)

procedure_steps.detail: Check eligibility: mainly PAYE income in previous 4 years; set up a new company carrying on a qualifying trade
Invest cash for new shares, take up employment in the company, and claim via Revenue (RICT/Form 11 through ROS)

documents_required.doc: Evidence of investment in new shares
Business plan showing job creation or R&D

eligibility.income_note: No income ceiling; for the 3 years before the year preceding investment, non-PAYE earnings must not exceed EUR50,000 or your employment income (whichever is lower)

programmes.source_snippet: SURE is a tax relief that provides a refund of Income Tax that you paid in previous years.

programmes.amount_note: Tax credit of up to EUR2,000 (the lower of EUR2,000 or 20% of qualifying earned income) for self-employed people, proprietary directors and others with earned income not covered by the Employee (PAYE) Tax Credit; combined value of Employee and Earned Income credits cannot exceed EUR2,000
programmes.deadline_note: Claim via myAccount for the current year or backdate up to 4 years

procedure_steps.detail: Sign into Revenue myAccount, open 'Claim tax credits' (current year) or 'Review Your Tax' (previous 4 years) and add the Earned Income Credit

eligibility.income_note: Not means-tested; available to anyone with qualifying earned (non-PAYE) income; full credit needs EUR10,000+ of earned income (20% rule)

programmes.source_snippet: The credit available is the lower of: €2,000 or 20% of your qualifying earned income.

programmes.funder: Local authorities with Approved Housing Bodies / approved private companies
programmes.amount_note: Homeowners in unsustainable mortgage arrears (after completing MARP with their lender) surrender ownership; an AHB or approved company buys the home and rents it back at an affordable, income-based social rent; option to buy back after 5 years; property value caps (e.g. EUR515,000 house in Dublin/Cork/Galway etc.) and positive-equity caps (EUR40,000-50,000) apply since 1 November 2024

procedure_steps.detail: Engage with your lender and complete the Mortgage Arrears Resolution Process (MARP)
Apply for social housing support with your local authority (income limits apply)
Complete the Mortgage to Rent application with your lender; get legal advice (lender pays up to EUR500)

documents_required.doc: Mortgage account and MARP completion evidence

documents_required.note: must be made before the MTR application

eligibility.income_note: Net household income must not exceed limits that depend on area and household composition (social housing income limits table); property value limits apply (e.g. house €515,000 in Dublin, Kildare, Meath, Wicklow, Louth, Cork and Galway; €395,000 elsewhere)

programmes.source_snippet: You must have a long-term right to remain in the State.

programmes.name_local: Iasacht Ceannaigh agus Athchóirithe Údaráis Áitiúil
programmes.name_en: Local Authority Purchase and Renovation Loan (LAPR)
programmes.amount_note: Government-backed mortgage to buy AND renovate a derelict or non-habitable home: fixed rates 4.00% (25 yrs) / 4.05% (30 yrs) plus a 3.50% variable bridging loan equal to the Vacant Property Refurbishment Grant (Croi Conaithe, up to EUR70,000) repayable when the grant is paid; you must qualify for the Vacant Property Refurbishment Grant and meet Local Authority Home Loan conditions (first-time buyer or fresh start, two insufficient bank offers, 10% deposit)

procedure_steps.detail: Check eligibility (income, first-time buyer/fresh start, 2 years continuous employment) and get two insufficient-offer letters from banks
Apply to the local authority where the property is located, with Vacant Property Refurbishment Grant eligibility

documents_required.doc: Two letters of insufficient finance offers from regulated lenders
Proof of income and 2 years certified accounts if self-employed

eligibility.income_note: Gross annual income below EUR80,000 for single applicants (from 1 April 2026; previously EUR70,000) and EUR85,000 for joint applicants

programmes.source_snippet: Increased income limit for all single applicants in each local authority area: increase from €70,000 to €80,000 for all single applicants.

programmes.name_local: Seirbhís um Chomhairle Airgid agus Buiséadú (MABS)
programmes.amount_note: Free, confidential, independent money advice and budgeting service (60+ offices nationwide plus helpline 0818 07 2000): help with debt, bills, utility and mortgage arrears, budgeting tools, and the Abhaile scheme (free expert financial/legal advice for people in home mortgage arrears, incl. vouchers for Personal Insolvency Practitioners)

procedure_steps.detail: Call the helpline 0818 07 2000 (Mon-Fri 9am-8pm), email helpline@mabs.ie or visit a local MABS office

eligibility.income_note: No means test for the advice service; targeted at people on low incomes or with problem debt

programmes.source_snippet: Our service is free of charge. Helpline 0818 07 2000

programmes.name_en: Society of St Vincent de Paul (SVP) assistance
programmes.funder: Society of St Vincent de Paul (charity)
programmes.amount_note: Ireland's largest voluntary charitable organisation; local volunteer Conferences provide once-off or short-term help with food, energy bills, education costs and other essentials after a home visit; help is discretionary and needs-based

procedure_steps.detail: Request help online at svp.ie/get-help or contact your local SVP Conference
SVP volunteers arrange a home visit to understand your situation and agree assistance

eligibility.income_note: Discretionary and needs-based rather than a fixed income threshold; assistance is for people in financial hardship

programmes.source_snippet: We assist individuals in need, regardless of faith, ethnicity, status, or sexual orientation.

programmes.name_en: TFI Local Link rural transport services
programmes.amount_note: Low-cost rural bus services (Regular Rural Services on fixed routes and pre-bookable Door-to-Door services) connecting villages and towns where other public transport is limited; distance-based fares (many trips under EUR3 on new demand-responsive services), TFI Leap Card and TFI Go app give 30% off, Free Travel pass accepted; Young Adult (19-25) and Student Leap Card holders get 50% off

procedure_steps.detail: Find your local TFI Local Link office/routes (15 regional coordination units) on transportforireland.ie
For door-to-door services, pre-book by phone/app (ideally the day before); pay by cash, Leap Card (30% off) or TFI Go app

eligibility.income_note: No income test; fares are subsidised and concession cards (Free Travel, Young Adult/Student Leap 50%) apply

programmes.source_snippet: Yes – the Free Travel Pass is accepted on all TFI Local Link Services.

programmes.name_local: Scéim Deontas Pobail Chathair Bhaile Átha Cliath
programmes.name_en: Dublin City Council Community Grants Scheme
programmes.amount_note: Annual grants to community and voluntary groups in the Dublin City Council area for local projects promoting social inclusion (2026 scheme fund EUR386,500); related supports include the Community Enhancement Programme/Local Enhancement Programme, Ballymun Social Regeneration Fund and Community Arts grants
programmes.deadline_note: 2026 scheme opened 22 January 2026 and closed 13:00 on 20 February 2026 (total fund €386,500); next round not yet announced

procedure_steps.detail: Check the annual call on dublincity.ie and apply via the Citizen's Hub before the deadline

documents_required.note: applicants must be community/voluntary groups, not individuals

eligibility.income_note: No income test; open to community and voluntary groups operating in the Dublin City area

programmes.source_snippet: The 2026 scheme opened for applications on Thursday 22nd January 2026 from 12 noon with a total fund of €386,500

programmes.amount_note: If approved you pay a fixed contribution (set by a financial assessment) towards long-term nursing home care and the HSE pays the balance of the approved cost. Funding is not backdated. An optional nursing home loan can be applied for as part of the application. Does not cover short-term care or extra fees such as hairdressing, therapies or activities.
programmes.deadline_note: Funding is only paid from the date it is approved and cannot be backdated.

procedure_steps.detail: Complete the Fair Deal application form
HSE arranges a care needs assessment to see if you need long-term nursing home care
HSE arranges a financial assessment to work out how much you pay

documents_required.doc: Completed Nursing Homes Support Scheme application form

eligibility.income_note: No fixed income ceiling: a financial assessment of your income and assets sets how much you contribute, and a 3 year cap applies to homes, farms and businesses. Approval also requires a care needs assessment showing you need long-term nursing home care.

programmes.source_snippet: If you're approved for Fair Deal, you pay a certain amount towards the total cost of nursing home care and HSE pays the balance.

programmes.amount_note: Once-off double week payment: in 2025 the Bonus was 100% of your normal weekly payment, with a minimum Bonus of €20. Paid in the first week of December to people getting a long-term social welfare payment. Not paid with Fuel Allowance alone. If you get 2 eligible payments you get the Bonus for both.
programmes.deadline_note: Paid automatically in the first week of December with your social welfare payment.

procedure_steps.detail: No application needed: you are paid automatically with your qualifying payment

eligibility.income_note: No separate income test: entitlement follows getting a qualifying long-term social welfare payment (for example State Pension, Disability Allowance, Carer's Allowance, One-Parent Family Payment, or Jobseeker's Allowance for 12 months).

programmes.source_snippet: The Christmas Bonus is a once-off double week payment for people getting a long-term social welfare payment.

programmes.name_local: Disabled Drivers and Disabled Passengers Tax Relief Scheme
programmes.name_en: Disabled Drivers and Disabled Passengers Tax Relief Scheme
programmes.amount_note: Remission or repayment of Value-Added Tax (VAT) and Vehicle Registration Tax (VRT) on a specially constructed or adapted vehicle, capped at €10,000, €16,000, €22,000, €32,000 or €48,000 depending on the category of adaptations and whether the Primary Medical Certificate holder is the driver or passenger. Also a fuel grant (up to 2,730 litres a year for a driver or passenger, 4,100 for an organisation) and possible motor tax exemption.
programmes.deadline_note: Only one vehicle can qualify per driver or passenger at any given time.

procedure_steps.detail: Get a Primary Medical Certificate (PMC) showing certain severe and permanent physical disabilities
Submit Form DD1 online through myAccount or ROS ('Drivers and Passengers with Disabilities' under Vehicle Services), or post a paper form to the Central Repayments Office, Limerick
Claim the fuel grant online with form FG1

eligibility.income_note: Not income-tested. Requires a Primary Medical Certificate (certain severe and permanent physical disabilities) and a vehicle specially constructed or adapted to carry the PMC holder.

programmes.source_snippet: A person must have certain severe and permanent physical disabilities to obtain a PMC.

programmes.amount_note: HSE funding for home care hours, allocated after a needs assessment based on the level of care you require. You can ask for Consumer Directed Home Support (CDHS), where you choose your provider and arrange the timing of calls and HSE pays the funding to your chosen provider.
programmes.deadline_note: You can apply at home, in hospital (ask the person managing your discharge plan) or from a nursing home if you want to return home.

procedure_steps.detail: Get the home support application form online or from your local home support office
