Fill in the form yourself or ask a family member, GP, nurse or other healthcare professional to complete it for you
Post the form to your local home support office
HSE carries out a needs assessment; if approved you are allocated funding

documents_required.doc: Completed Home Support Service application form
documents_required.note: Declaration and consent in part 12 must be signed by you or a person legally allowed to act for you

eligibility.income_note: No income ceiling is published on the how-to-apply page; the service is allocated on assessed care needs.

programmes.source_snippet: You can apply for the Home Support Service if you are:

Funding is allocated to the college, not the student; your college organises supports with you.
programmes.deadline_note: Register with your college's disability or access office as soon as possible; students do not apply directly to the HEA.

procedure_steps.detail: Register with the disability or access office in your college
Meet the college's criteria and have your support needs verified
Your college arranges services, supports or equipment in consultation with you

documents_required.doc: Evidence of a verifiable disability in one of the HEA categories (for example autism, ADHD, dyslexia, deaf or hard of hearing, mental health condition)

eligibility.income_note: Not income-tested. You must have a verifiable disability, a verified need for supports, be legally resident in Ireland for at least 3 of the 5 years before your course starts, and be an Irish, EU, EEA, UK or Swiss national (non-EU nationals eligible for free or reduced fees under the Free Fees Initiative may also be considered).

programmes.source_snippet: The FSD is one of the main funding sources supporting participation by students with disabilities in approved higher education courses in Ireland.

programmes.amount_note: Maximum €2,000 for 2026. Full amount if your yearly PAYE income (employment or pension income) is €10,000 or more; if below €10,000 the credit is capped at 20% of that income. If you and your spouse or civil partner both have PAYE income, you can each claim it. You cannot transfer it. Only one Employee Tax Credit regardless of how many jobs.
programmes.deadline_note: You can claim for the current year or the previous 4 years through myAccount.

procedure_steps.detail: Sign in to Revenue myAccount
Under 'PAYE Services' choose 'Manage your Tax for the current year' then 'Claim tax credits'

eligibility.income_note: No income ceiling: the credit is full at PAYE income of €10,000 or more and is capped at 20% of PAYE income below that. Not available to proprietary directors on directorship income, or to the spouse, civil partner or child of the person paying the income (with exceptions).

programmes.source_snippet: The maximum employee tax credit for 2026 is €2,000.

procedure_steps.detail: Fill in the Disablement Benefit claim form OB21
Post it to the Disablement Benefit Section, Department of Social Protection, Social Welfare Services Office, Government Buildings, Ballinalee Road, Longford
A Department medical assessor decides your level of disablement

eligibility.income_note: Not means-tested: a compensation payment disregarded for most means tests (counted for Supplementary Welfare Allowance and Working Family Payment). Requires insurable employment (PRSI Class A, B, D, J or M) when the accident or disease occurred and disablement of 15% or more.

programmes.source_snippet: Payment is only made where the level of disablement following the accident or disease is assessed at 15% or more.

programmes.amount_note: Legal advice and representation in civil matters (such as family law) provided by Law Centres; you may have to pay a contribution (see the Legal Aid Board contributions page). Financial eligibility is a disposable income test and the Board also applies a merits test.
programmes.deadline_note: Waiting times vary by Law Centre.

procedure_steps.detail: Check your financial eligibility with the online calculator
Complete the online application form or contact your local Law Centre

eligibility.income_note: You must have disposable income under €18,000 (income left after deducting allowances such as tax, accommodation costs and childcare). Not household gross income: the Board also assesses assets and applies a merits test.

programmes.source_snippet: To qualify for Legal Aid Services you must have disposable income under €18,000.

programmes.amount_note: 2026 amounts: single person €2,000; married person or civil partner €4,000; widowed person or surviving civil partner €2,540 without dependent children or €2,000 with; year of death €4,000; Widowed Parent credit €3,600 in the 1st year after death falling to €1,800 in the 5th year.
programmes.deadline_note: Claim through Revenue myAccount.

procedure_steps.detail: Sign in to Revenue myAccount and make sure your marital status and tax credits are correct

eligibility.income_note: No income ceiling: due to anyone resident in Ireland for tax purposes; amount depends on marital or civil status.

programmes.source_snippet: You are due a Personal Tax Credit if you are resident in Ireland.

programmes.amount_note: Supplementary income for low-income farmers and fishers: minimum weekly payment €286.50 (for Jobseeker's Allowance, Farm Assist, Fish Assist or One-Parent Family Payment recipients this is €254 plus a €32.50 top-up; recipients of Disability Allowance and certain pensions keep their payment with a top-up of at least €32.50). Participants work 19.5 hours a week on a farmer- or fisher-friendly schedule.

procedure_steps.detail: Contact your local Implementing Body for information and an application form
Provide proof you are actively farming at least 1 hectare (BISS application with farming number) or fishing (licence documentation)

documents_required.doc: Basic Income Support for Sustainability (BISS) application with farming number, or fishing evidence
RSS2 form (Use of Farming Number/Fishing Licence Agreement)
documents_required.note: Needed for the defined connection or couples route

eligibility.income_note: The same means rules that apply to your original qualifying social welfare payment also apply, so no separate income figure is published on the RSS page. programmes.source_snippet: The Rural Social Scheme provides a supplementary income for low-income farmers and fishers who are unable to earn an adequate living.

programmes.name_local: Government of Ireland International Education Scholarship
programmes.name_en: Government of Ireland International Education Scholarship (GOI-IES)

Apply on the HEA online portal when the annual call is open

documents_required.doc: Conditional or final offer of admission

programmes.source_snippet: A Government of Ireland International Education Scholarship consists of a stipend amounting to €10,000 for one year of full-time study at NFQ levels 9 or 10.

programmes.deadline_note: Apply online once your course has started

Collect your card from a Student Leap Card agent after the confirmation email

International students: acceptance letter from the Irish university

programmes.source_snippet: Full time international students who meet the criteria above are also entitled to apply for the Student Leap Card whilst in Ireland.
